chapters.summary: Chair Williams opens the hearing and introduces Proposed Intro 220-A, sponsored by Majority Whip Hanks, which would require the city to identify and commemorate historical African-American burial sites. She notes a recent incident in Queens where such a site was paved over, underscoring the bill's relevance.
chapters.title: Chair Williams opens hearing and introduces African American burial sites bill

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: We are back again.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: I am Deputy Speaker Nantasha Williams, Chair of the Committee on Cultural Affairs, Libraries, and International Relations.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Today, the committee will vote on one bill and three resolutions, which have already been heard.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Proposed intro number 220A, sponsored by Majority Whip Kamillah-Hanks, a local law which would amend the administrative code of the City of New York in relations to a report regarding the identification and commemoration of historical

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: African-American burial sites.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: And I just wanted to note that there is an active.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: situation happening in Queens where an African-American burial site was paved over.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: So this is quite relevant.

chapters.summary: Chair Williams introduces Resolution 82-A, sponsored by Councilmember Amanda Farías, which would celebrate the Feast of San Gennaro and Ferragosto Festival annually in September to honor Italian immigrants and Italian Americans' contributions to New York City.
chapters.title: Chair Williams introduces San Gennaro and Ferragosto resolution

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: The next is a resolution by Councilmember Amanda Farías, number

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: 82A, which would celebrate the Feast of San Gennaro and Ferragusto Festival annually in September to honor the contributions of Italian immigrants and Italian Americans to the cultural, political, and economic fabric of the city of New York.

chapters.summary: Chair Williams introduces Resolution 402, her own resolution declaring March 6 as Carmen de Lavallade Day in New York City, celebrating her contributions to dance, theater, diversity, and artistic excellence in the performing arts.
chapters.title: Chair Williams introduces Carmen de Lavallade Day resolution

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Resolution number 402, sponsored by myself, which would declare March 6th as Carmen de la Valade in the city of New York

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: to celebrate her life and legacy and to honor her groundbreaking contributions to dance and theater, as well as her role in advancing diversity and artistic excellence in the performing arts.

chapters.summary: Chair Williams introduces Resolution 429, also sponsored by herself, recognizing the life and legacy of Alvin Ailey and honoring his contributions to American dance and the founding of the Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater.
chapters.title: Chair Williams introduces Alvin Ailey legacy resolution

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: And resolution number 429, also sponsored by myself, which will recognize the life and legacy of Alvin Ailey and honor his contributions to American dance and the founding of the Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater.

chapters.summary: Chair Williams introduces Resolution 6, sponsored by the Speaker, commemorating the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks, and Proposed Resolution 237-A, sponsored by Councilmember Crystal Hudson, calling on Congress to pass the Performing Artist Tax Parity Act.
chapters.title: Chair Williams introduces 9/11 anniversary and Performing Artist Tax Parity resolutions

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Additionally, the committee will hear and vote on resolution six, sponsored by the speaker, which would commemorate the 25th anniversary of the September 11 attacks and proposed resolution.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: 237A sponsored by Councilmember Crystal Hudson, which would call on the United States Congress to pass and the president to sign the Performing Artist Tax Parity Act.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: First, I will turn to Councilmember Hudson to deliver remarks on her resolution.

chapters.summary: Councilmember Crystal Hudson delivers remarks on her resolution calling on Congress to pass the Performing Artist Tax Parity Act, arguing that working artists are essential to New York City's culture and economy and deserve a tax system reflecting their realities. She urges colleagues to vote aye.
chapters.title: Councilmember Hudson advocates for Performing Artist Tax Parity Act resolution

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Chair Dr.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Williams.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Working artists are an essential part of the fabric of New York City's culture and economy, and they deserve a tax system that reflects the realities of making a living in this field.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: I'm proud that the council is voicing our support for the Performing Artists Tax Parity Act and is calling on Congress to give working artists the support they need to keep creating and contributing to our city, and I urge my colleagues to vote aye.

utterances.speaker: Crystal Hudson
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Sure and sweet.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Next.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Yes, very true.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Just like you.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Next up, Councilmember Farias.

chapters.summary: Councilmember Amanda Farías presents Resolution 82, celebrating the Feast of San Gennaro and Ferragosto Festival in Manhattan's Little Italy and the Bronx's Arthur Avenue. She describes the festivals as living histories of Italian immigrant families and notes it took a year to get the resolution on the calendar.
chapters.title: Councilmember Farías on celebrating Feast of San Gennaro and Ferragosto

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Good morning and thank you, Chair Williams and the members of the Committee on Cultural Affairs, Libraries and International Relations.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: I'm Councilmember Amanda Farias and I'm proud.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Apologies.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Proud to be here before you as we vote on my resolution 82.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: This resolution would formally recognize and celebrate the Feast of San Gennaro and the Ferragasso

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Festival, two key festivals of this city, our Little Italies in Manhattan and the Bronx, and the wider Italian community each September, while simultaneously honoring the contributions of Italian immigrants and Italian Americans to New York City.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: These festivals are more than beloved neighborhood traditions.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: They can carry forward the histories that Italian families have brought to New York and passed down through generations.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: The Feast of San Gennaro has welcomed New Yorkers to many...

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Manhattan's Little Italy for over a century, while Ferragosto brings thousands of people together along Arthur Avenue to celebrate the food, music, businesses, culture, and families that have shaped our Bronx communities.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: New York City's identity was built by immigrant communities that preserve their traditions while helping shape the city around them.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Resolution 82 recognizes that Italian American history in New York City

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: is New York City history and ensures that these celebrations remain part of our city's cultural calendar for generations to come.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: Thank you to my colleagues who have joined me in sponsoring this resolution and who will join in passage.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: It's taken a year to get this on the calendar and I'm really excited to get it done, both for our Italian Americans across the city, but specifically in the Bronx as well.

utterances.speaker: Amanda C. Farías
utterances.text: And I respectfully ask all of my colleagues today in committee to vote yes.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: It's because the chair studied abroad in Italy for six months.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: I'm just kidding.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: It's not why.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Next up, we have Majority Whip, who would also like to give remarks on her bill.

chapters.summary: Majority Whip Kamillah Hanks delivers remarks on Intro 220-A, thanking scholars, advocates, and descendants who pushed the bill forward. She explains the bill gives the city responsibility to locate, document, protect, and recognize historical African-American burial sites, calling it one important step toward a larger promise.
chapters.title: Majority Whip Hanks on African American burial sites bill

utterances.speaker: Kamillah Hanks
utterances.text: Thank you, Dr.

utterances.speaker: Kamillah Hanks
utterances.text: Chair Williams, Speaker Menon, and my colleagues.

utterances.speaker: Kamillah Hanks
utterances.text: I also want to thank the scholars, the advocates.

utterances.speaker: Kamillah Hanks
utterances.text: descendants, community leaders, and everyone whose knowledge and persistence brought this work forward.

utterances.speaker: Kamillah Hanks
utterances.text: New York cannot tell its complete story while the resting places of people remain unseen.

utterances.speaker: Kamillah Hanks
utterances.text: These New Yorkers have lived here, worked here, built communities here, and helped build the city we inherit today.

utterances.speaker: Kamillah Hanks
utterances.text: Their lives deserve dignity.

utterances.speaker: Kamillah Hanks
utterances.text: Their resting places deserve dignity.

utterances.speaker: Kamillah Hanks
utterances.text: protection, and their descendants deserve to know what their history matters.

utterances.speaker: Kamillah Hanks
utterances.text: Intro 220A gives the city a responsibility to locate, document, protect, and recognize these sites guided by scholarship, oral histories, and community knowledge.

utterances.speaker: Kamillah Hanks
utterances.text: This bill is not the end of that work.

utterances.speaker: Kamillah Hanks
utterances.text: It is one important step towards a larger promise that will not erase a New Yorker from our shared memory.

utterances.speaker: Kamillah Hanks
utterances.text: And today we take that step together.

utterances.speaker: Kamillah Hanks
utterances.text: And I hope that my colleagues will vote for this bill today.

utterances.speaker: Kamillah Hanks
utterances.text: We will continue this work until every part of our history is seen, honored, and never forgotten.

utterances.speaker: Kamillah Hanks
utterances.text: Thank you, Chair.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Thank you.

chapters.summary: Chair Williams delivers remarks on her two resolutions honoring Carmen de Lavallade and Alvin Ailey, describing how they met in high school in Los Angeles, how de Lavallade brought Ailey to Lester Horton's dance classes, and their early years dancing together in Horton's racially integrated company.
chapters.title: Chair Williams on de Lavallade and Ailey's early partnership and California years

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Finally, let me say a few words about my two resolutions honoring the lives and work of Carmen de la Valade and Alvin Ailey.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: It is fitting that these two resolutions be voted on together because it is likely that there is no Alvin Ailey without Carmen de la Valade.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: After they met in high school in Los Angeles, Miss de la Valade took young Alvin to her dance classes at Lester Horton Studio.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: He loved watching her in class and eventually Lester Horton asked young Alvin if he would like to take classes as well.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: He enthusiastically agreed and the rest is history.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Lester Horton, who pioneered the modern Horton technique that is still danced by the Alvin Ailey American Dance Theater and is taught in the Ailey School, had a small racially integrated company where Mr.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Lavallade and Mr.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Ailey first danced together.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: After Mr.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Horton's untimely death, the two young dancers took over the company and tried hard to make it work, which was very difficult.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: When New York City beckoned, they left California together to come dance on Broadway.

chapters.summary: Chair Williams continues her remarks, describing how de Lavallade and Ailey moved to New York to dance on Broadway, Ailey's founding of his own company, his choreography of roles for de Lavallade including in Revelations, and their long and brilliant careers. She thanks committee staff before calling the roll.
chapters.title: Chair Williams on Ailey's company, Revelations, and the legacies of both artists

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: When Mr.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Ailey started his own tiny dance company, he choreographed roles for his favorite partner, including an iconic role for her in his signature ballet of 1960, Revelations.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: I love Revelations.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Revelations is the story of what Mr.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Earley called his blood memories.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Other words, his memories of growing up in a small town of Rogers, Texas, where he watched workers picking cotton and where he attended church with his beloved mother on Sundays.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Set to traditional spirituals, Revelations is also the story of the trials and tribulations, as well as the joys of the African-American experience.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Both Mr.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Lavallade and Mr.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Ailey had long and brilliant careers, dancing and choreographing across the world for many prestigious companies, including Mr.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Ailey's own company, and winning honor after honor.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: Their artistic legacies will never be forgotten here in New York City, which they made their home.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: I would like to thank my staff and committee staff who worked on preparing for today, including Alejandro, the committee's counsel who drafted the bill, and Regina Paul, the committee's senior policy analyst who drafted four of the resolutions.

utterances.speaker: Nantasha M. Williams
utterances.text: And with that, I will ask the clerk to call the roll.

summary: The Committee on Cultural Affairs, Libraries and International Relations voted on one bill (Int 220-A) requiring the city to identify and commemorate historical African-American burial sites, and five resolutions honoring Italian American cultural festivals, Carmen de Lavallade and Alvin Ailey's dance legacies, the 25th anniversary of 9/11, and federal Performing Artist Tax Parity legislation.

Councilmembers Hudson, Farías, and Hanks each delivered remarks on their respective items, while Chair Williams introduced the agenda and spoke at length on the interconnected legacies of Carmen de Lavallade and Alvin Ailey.
All items passed by a vote of 7-0 with no abstentions, with the full committee present.
title: Committee on Cultural Affairs, Libraries and International Relations
topic: A report and map of historical African American burial sites
